thread:
amelia: hi all, new hire here! quick q: where should I put my dev ssh key for deployment testing? I was told not to commit it.
raj: welcome! we don't store personal SSH keys in Vault by default. what's your workflow? local push or CI?
amelia: mostly CI-driven deploys and occasional debug on staging. team is infra-deploy.
raj: for CI we prefer using a deploy service account with an SSH key stored in Vault under `secret/data/ci/keys/<service>` and the CI reads it at job time. for interactive debug, use your workstation key + allowed bastion.
amelia: ok. curious about KMS - we also have KMS keys for encrypting secrets at rest. when do we use KMS vs Vault?
june_security: short answer: KMS (cloud KMS) -> key management and envelope encryption; Vault -> secret storage, leasing, dynamic creds. Use KMS for encrypting blobs or wrapping keys, use Vault for storing credentials, API keys, SSH keys, and minting short-lived DB creds.
sre-oncall: for deploys we typically: 1) put encrypted SSH key in Vault, 2) enable TTL and rotation, 3) CI fetches and uses ephemeral agent. If you need to create a SA with key json for GCP, use workload identity instead of long lived key when possible.
amelia: what about rotation? who rotates SSH keys in Vault and how often?
june_security: rotation policy: service keys stored under `secret/data/sa/` or `secret/data/ci/keys/` get monthly rotation by automation. If your service has a dependency that can't support rotation, tag the secret with `no-rotation` and include business justification; that requires sec approval and is temporary. User/dev keys should be rotated by the owner and not stored centrally.
amelia: got it. I need access to `secret/data/ci/keys/infra-deploy` for my CI. who do I ask?
raj: open the onboarding access form at https://intranet.redwood.com/onboard/secrets and choose "Vault read/write for CI". add the repo, the CI pipeline id, and list approvers (team owners + infra security).
amelia: submitted form: request 2026-ONB-900. how long till access?
devex-bot: Your request 2026-ONB-900 has been submitted. SLA: Vault read/write for CI within 1 business day after approvals; KMS IAM changes up to 48 hours. Reply with approver names if faster grant needed.
sre-oncall: pinging infra-deploy owners now. also include `secrets-mint` in the ticket if you want ephemeral creds instead of storing keys.
amelia: thanks. once access is granted how do I check?
raj: run `vault login -method=oidc` then `vault kv get secret/data/ci/keys/infra-deploy` should return the secret. `vault token lookup` shows attached policies. if you see `permission denied` run `vault auth list` and confirm method.
june_security: and check audit logs if something looks off: https://internal-logs.redwood.com/audit/vault. reach out to security if you see unexpected policy changes.
amelia: great. last Q: any templates for the ticket justification?
raj: copy this: "CI pipeline infra-deploy needs SSH private key to perform automated deployments to staging. Repo: git.redwood.com/infra/deploy. Approvers: infra-deploy-owner1, infra-deploy-owner2. Access type: read (CI) + rotate monthly."
amelia: perfect. thanks y'all :pray:
sre-oncall: welcome aboard :tada: we'll follow up in the ticket.
june_security: if you want a quick 15-min runthrough on secrets best practices, DM me and I'll schedule.
amelia: will do, appreciate it!
